Q: How to generate a simple ARIMA process with statsmodels A:

Your code doesn't work because this line model = ARIMA([0], order=order) fits an ARIMA model with one data point (value = 0), which doesn't make sense. If you want to simulate data using AR/MA parameters, you should define ArmaProcess and call generate_sample() .

It is detailed in statsmodels documentation: https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/generated/statsmodels.tsa.arima_process.ArmaProcess.html

Working code:

import numpy as np
import statsmodels.api as sm

ar_params = np.array([0.4])
ma_params = np.array([-0.2])

ar = np.r_[1, -ar_params]
ma = np.r_[1, ma_params]

arma_process = sm.tsa.ArmaProcess(ar, ma)
y = arma_process.generate_sample(50000)

Q: ODBC varchar(max) parameter seems to throw "HY104 - Invalid precision value" for 8000 characters A:

Although I still haven't determined the exact cause, I found that setting the Size field on the OdbcParameter to the actual size of the data appears to fix the issue.

Tested with values of exactly 8000 and below and above that too, just to verify.

Q: Running sh or bash script commands from the bottom to the top A:

let cmd.sh be:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
cmd1
cmd2
cmd3

for reverse run use:

cat cmd.sh | (sed -u 1q; tac)

which yields:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
cmd3
cmd2
cmd1

to run the reverse:

cat cmd.sh | (sed -u 1q; tac) | sh

The warnings about multi line scripts etc. apply

Q: How can I kill a process when a specific string is seen on standard error? A:

WARNING: This solution has a couple small but potentially very confusing problems; don't use it as it. A revision is on the way.

Zombo's answer is lovely but I wanted to be able to use it from a script. So here's a version that doesn't write to /dev/tty and returns a error code if the specified pattern is seen on stderr or the command fails:

function do_halting_on_stderr_matching
{
  local cmd="$1"
  local error_regex="$2"

  while true
  do
    if read -r -t 0.1; then
      if [[ $REPLY =~ $error_regex ]]; then
        echo got error line: "$REPLY" >&2
        kill $!
        return 1
      else
        echo $REPLY
      fi
    fi
    if ! kill -0 $! 2>/dev/null; then
      wait $!
      return $?
    fi
  done < <( $cmd 2>&1 )
}

do_halting_on_stderr_matching "./two_warning_script.sh some args" "warning: "

I also didn't use exec to run the $cmd, which might mean it doesn't support redirection in the command itself (I'm not sure what exec is intended for in Zombo's answer).

The two_warning_script.sh used to test this could look like this:

#!/bin/sh

echo warning: type1 >&2
sleep 2
echo warning: type2 >&2
echo handled args "$@"

This is convenient for scripting involving long-running commands that can be aborted early if a particular warning (or any other stderr matching the pattern)

Q: GWT-JSNI passing a JavaScriptObject in an external JS library A:

The problem is that GWT code runs in an iframe (for sandboxing/isolation) and Anno only supports array types from the same browsing context.

See http://perfectionkills.com/instanceof-considered-harmful-or-how-to-write-a-robust-isarray/ and http://web.mit.edu/jwalden/www/isArray.html for descriptions of the problem.

ECMAScript 5.1 added an Array.isArray() function that solves that issue and has wide browser support (back up to IE9): https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/isArray
And jQuery has one too, which makes it incomprehensible (to me) that Anno doesn't use it instead of using the broken if arg.__proto__ is Array.prototype (unless it's by design). So first things first: file an issue on Anno.

As a workaround, it should be possible to use $wnd.Array.apply($wnd.Array, steps) to copy your array into an array from the top window.
